pr_title: drivers: wdog: fix wrong logic in NXP drivers
pr_body:
This pull request fixes #79178 

The wdog driver for NXP implements a wrong logic for the sleep and debug bits.
It does not stop the wdog if in debug or sleep state, leading to a false trigger.

issue_context.title: Wrong logic in NXP driver for watchdog
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**

I am working on a i.MX from NXP and implemented the watchdog using the Zephyr API. During development the watchdog was not behaving as expected and I looked into the driver code and probably found a bug

**To Reproduce**

**In the following file the logic is wrong. The watchdog options for sleep and debug get set when the corresponding bit is 0, which is not correct according the [Zephyr API](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/doxygen/html/group__watchdog__interface.html).**

https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/2815b6d710ad9c7ba25725ae34c402fc9153c427/drivers/watchdog/wdt_mcux_imx_wdog.c#L44-L48

I corrected it for my i.MX RT, but found two more files in Zephyr 3.6 where this issue is also existent:

https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/2815b6d710ad9c7ba25725ae34c402fc9153c427/drivers/watchdog/wdt_mcux_wdog.c#L45-L49

https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/2815b6d710ad9c7ba25725ae34c402fc9153c427/drivers/watchdog/wdt_mcux_wdog32.c#L53-L57

**Expected behavior**

The correct way would be invert the logic, just like this:

```
 data->wdog_config.workMode.enableStop = 
 	(options & WDT_OPT_PAUSE_IN_SLEEP) == WDT_OPT_PAUSE_IN_SLEEP; 
  
 data->wdog_config.workMode.enableDebug = 
 	(options & WDT_OPT_PAUSE_HALTED_BY_DBG) == WDT_OPT_PAUSE_HALTED_BY_DBG; 
```
I fixed it locally, but it would be nice to have it in the next Zephyr release included :) 

**Impact**

The watchdog runs just fine and also triggers fine. But it does not stop when the device is put to sleep, which can cause miss-triggers. Also when debugging the code and halting the core wit the debugger the watchdog also triggers.

This is annyoing, especially when you don't know the cause of the reset. 

**Logs and console output**

N/A

**Environment (please complete the following information):**

Probably all i.MX processors, also all S32 processors. I am not sure, which processor are using the file `wdt_mcux_wdog.c` and `wdt_mxuc_wdog32.c`, but this bug could have a big scope

**Should I create a PR for this to be fixed? I can open one for the 3 above mentioned files**
comments: If you could submit a PR, that'd be great. If these bugs are confirmed, they should be backported too.
This bug was with v3.6 but was fixed in v3.7

review_comments:
So the documentation in the iMX RT1024 RM for the watchdog WDBG bit says the following:

> The WDOG timer can be configured for continual operation, or for suspension during
debug mode. If the WDOG debug enable (WDBG) bit is set in the Watchdog Control
(WCR), the WDOG timer operation is suspended in debug mode.

Setting the `enableDebug` field to true for the MCUX `wdog01` driver will result in the `WDBG` bit being cleared: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/hal_nxp/blob/9702923eeb6f4a9ca063ca3b200324b118d3e843/mcux/mcux-sdk/drivers/wdog01/fsl_wdog.c#L112

So it seems that setting the `enableDebug` field for the MCUX driver will cause the watchdog to continue running in debug mode. Based on the documentation of the `WDT_OPT_PAUSE_HALTED_BY_DBG` bit: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/c82799bd4c2980f579afcb0b3dc07991f765579d/include/zephyr/drivers/watchdog.h#L38

It seems like the current behavior is correct, right?

Sorry for the delay. The bug wax fixed in Zephyr 3.7.0 and in a different place than I was looking, so I just overlooked it.
It was fixed in NXP SDK 2.15.0 which is used in zephyr 3.7

However, it still persists in older versions.

See this version of the file in zephyr 3.6.0:
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/hal_nxp/blob/d45b14c198d778658b7853b48378d2e132a6c4be/mcux/mcux-sdk/drivers/wdog01/fsl_wdog.c#L112

Should this be backported?

Should this be backported?

Ah, this is fun. The fix for the issue was effectively the SDK 2.15 update, but we cannot backport that. I *think* the best approach here would be the following:
- update the issue text to explicitly refer to 3.6, and highlight how the issue has been fixed in newer releases by the SDK update
- Create a PR targeting the 3.6 branch (and be explicit in the description as to how this issue only exists in 3.6, and not on main)

I suppose the other option we could pursue would be patching the 2.14 SDK watchdog driver, and syncing that change back to 3.6. I'd rather just change the logic within the Zephyr driver though, since that reduces the number of changes needed to fix this issue
I'm not sure it is worth going back to v3.6 to address as support for v3.6 ends next month.
